title: enrich_steps builds input_frames / source_names / source_ids with DIFFERENT filter predicates, so a missing/None parent output desynchronises the positional alignment and optimiserApply trace selects the wrong parent DataFrame (or raises a spurious index ValueError)
description: In the optimiserApply branch of enrich_steps the three positionally-correlated argument lists are derived from the same parent_ids list but with non-matching guards: input_frames keeps `pid` only when `pid in eager_outputs and eager_outputs[pid] is not None`, while source_names and source_ids keep `pid` when `pid in node_map`. A parent that failed to execute is ABSENT from eager_outputs (trace.py:768 builds `eager_outputs = {nid: df ... if df is not None}`, so failed/None nodes are dropped) but is still PRESENT in node_map (node_map holds every node). When such a parent precedes a real one, input_frames drops it while source_ids/source_names retain it, so the frames tuple is shorter than / shifted relative to source_ids. The downstream selector _select_optimiser_apply_input (_builders.py:1409-1415) does `index = source_ids.index(ratebook_input); return dfs[index]`, which assumes dfs and source_ids are positionally aligned. Result: in ratebook mode the wrong parent frame is selected, or `index >= len(dfs)` raises the misleading 'expected ratebook_input at index N but received M input(s)' ValueError; in online mode _select_optimiser_apply_input returns `dfs[0]`, so a dropped first parent silently makes dfs[0] the SECOND parent's frame, yielding a confidently-wrong optimiser explanation. The engine's own non-trace build path (_builders.py:1013-1016) deliberately rebuilds dfs in declared-source order to keep dfs/_src_names/_src_ids consistent; the trace path here does not, diverging from that contract. Because the call is wrapped in the per-node try/except, the failure surfaces as a node_detail error marker or a wrong explanation rather than a hard crash.
evidence: Lines 1724-1742: `parent_ids = parents_of.get(step.node_id, [])`; `input_frames = [eager_outputs[pid] for pid in parent_ids if pid in eager_outputs and eager_outputs[pid] is not None]`; `source_names = [_sanitize_func_name(node_map[pid].data.label) for pid in parent_ids if pid in node_map]`; `source_ids=[pid for pid in parent_ids if pid in node_map]`. The `eager_outputs[pid] is not None` guard proves the author anticipated absent/None frames, yet that filter is not applied to source_ids/source_names. _select_optimiser_apply_input (_builders.py:1383-1415) selects `dfs[0]` for online mode and `dfs[source_ids.index(ratebook_input)]` for ratebook mode, both requiring dfs[i] to correspond to source_ids[i]. eager_outputs values are never None / failed nodes are absent (trace.py:768), but node_map contains all nodes (trace.py:_assemble_steps reads node_map[nid] for every ordered node), so a failed/absent parent satisfies `pid in node_map` but not `pid in eager_outputs` — desynchronising the lists. Reachable on the partial-execution trace path (trace.py:514-524 assembles steps for nodes even when the target failed) and whenever an optimiserApply node has ≥1 parent missing from eager_outputs.
